seoTitle: How to Add Postage Costs on eBay (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Learn how to set shipping charges on eBay in 2026 — flat rate, calculated shipping, free shipping, or international postage — from desktop and mobile.
intro: Getting shipping costs right on eBay is a balancing act: charge too much and buyers bounce off your listing, charge too little and postage quietly eats your margin on every sale. eBay's Shipping Preferences page in Seller Hub is where most of that balance gets set, from which carrier rates you offer down to which countries you're willing to ship to at all. This guide walks through the actual settings on that page so you can set it up once and apply it across your listings instead of guessing on a per-item basis.

steps.heading: Find Shipping Preferences in Seller Hub
steps.body: From Seller Hub's account menu, open Shipping Preferences, which sits alongside Seller Account, Business Policies, and Selling Preferences in the left-hand list. This one page controls the shipping defaults that apply across your listings, rather than settings you'd otherwise have to repeat on every item you list.

steps.heading: Set your combined shipping rules
steps.body: Combined Shipping Rules determine how eBay calculates a single shipping charge when a buyer purchases multiple items from you at once — the page separates this into a flat shipping rule, a calculated shipping rule, and a promotional shipping rule, each editable on its own. Leaving these on "Not specified" means eBay falls back to charging full shipping per item, which usually costs you the sale when a buyer is filling a cart, so it's worth configuring at least one rule if you regularly sell multiples.

image.caption: The Shipping Preferences page in Seller Hub, showing Combined shipping rules, invoice request settings, and the Rates and exclusions section below it.

steps.heading: Choose your carrier rate settings
steps.body: Under Rates and Exclusions, Carrier Rate Settings lets you offer eBay's discounted carrier rates to buyers or provide your own custom discounted rate if you have a separate account with a carrier. Most sellers start with eBay's discounted rates since they require no extra setup and are usually competitive without needing to negotiate directly with a shipping provider.

steps.heading: Set shipping rate tables for domestic and international buyers
steps.body: Shipping rate tables let you define flat costs based on buyer region rather than typing a shipping price into every single listing — the same Rates and Exclusions section shows a table split by Domestic and International, both starting at zero until you configure them. Building these out once means new listings can just reference the table instead of you recalculating postage each time you list something new.

steps.heading: Exclude locations you won't ship to
steps.body: The Exclude Shipping Locations screen breaks the world into regions — Africa, Asia, Central America and Caribbean, Europe, the Middle East, North America, Oceania, South America, and Southeast Asia — each with checkboxes and a "Show all countries" link for finer control, plus a Domestic section covering Alaska and Hawaii, US APO/FPO, and US Protectorates. This is the honest way to avoid a listing going out to a country where shipping cost or customs complexity makes the sale not worth it, rather than manually canceling those orders after the fact.

image.caption: The Exclude Shipping Locations page, with checkboxes for domestic regions and a full breakdown of international zones by continent.

steps.heading: Decide between free shipping and a separate charge
steps.body: Once your rates and exclusions are set, you can fold shipping into the item price and mark the listing as free shipping, which commonly improves how listings rank in eBay search, or keep it broken out as its own line so buyers see the exact carrier cost. Testing both approaches on similar items is the only reliable way to know which converts better for what you specifically sell — margins on shipping-inclusive pricing behave differently by category and item weight.

steps.heading: Save it as a reusable business policy
steps.body: Rather than reconfiguring shipping on every new listing, save your settings as a Business Policy once you're happy with the rules, rate table, and exclusions. From then on, applying a shipping policy to a new listing takes one selection instead of rebuilding the whole setup, and updating the policy later automatically updates every listing that references it.

faq.question: Should I offer free shipping or charge separately on eBay?
faq.answer: Free shipping, with the cost folded into the item price, can boost search ranking, but a separate charge gives buyers more price transparency — test both on similar listings to see what performs better for your category.

faq.question: How does eBay calculate shipping cost?
faq.answer: Calculated shipping uses the weight and dimensions you enter, plus the buyer's delivery address, to pull live carrier rates rather than relying on a flat price you set manually.

faq.question: Can I set different shipping costs for different countries?
faq.answer: Yes — the Exclude Shipping Locations page lets you block regions entirely, and shipping rate tables let you set different flat costs for domestic versus international buyers.

faq.question: What happens if I don't set combined shipping rules?
faq.answer: Without a combined shipping rule configured, eBay defaults to charging full postage on every item in a multi-item order, which often discourages buyers from purchasing more than one thing from you at a time.

faq.question: Can I update shipping costs on a listing that's already live?
faq.answer: Yes, you can edit shipping details on active listings from Seller Hub without relisting the item, and any changes to a linked business policy apply automatically.
